message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on "Snow Fall" stone, which the lab found to be an igneous stone other than granite. Slabs of that kind, cut and polished, fall under heading 6802.

Heading 6802 covers worked monumental or building stone. Subheading 6802.93 covers granite, and 6802.99 covers other stone. Subheading 6802.91 covers marble, travertine and alabaster. Because the stone is igneous but not granite, it falls under 6802.99. Statistical suffix 6802.99.0090 is "other," under the "other stone" breakout.

Under 6802.99.00, the stone is "Other stone: Other." The 10-digit numbers are 6802.99.0010 (calcareous stone other than marble, travertine, alabaster, e.g., limestone), 6802.99.0020 (slate), and 6802.99.0090 (other). The "other" suffix fits the laboratory finding of an igneous stone that is not granite.

Duty rates are generally 6.5% for 6802.99.0090 versus 4% for some others. I'm not fully sure of the rate, but the classification stands.

I considered 6802.93 for polished granite, but the lab said "other igneous stone," which suggests it is not granite in the tariff sense. For example, CBP rulings about stones like this one often conclude that "the applicable subheading for Snow Fall will be 6802.99.0090."

{"hts_code": "6802.99.0090", "reason": "Polished slabs of an igneous stone that the laboratory determined is not granite are worked building stone classified in heading 6802 as other stone (6802.99), with the 'other' statistical suffix."}
